en: The Hymn to the Sixty-Four Samvaras:
I bow with my whole being to the glorious Heruka, the great hero, the pure Lord of the Vajra, adorned by the host of ḍākinīs. (1)
Homage to you, the vow; homage again and again to you who possess a twofold form.
Homage to you, the deity residing in the wheel, O Cakrasaṃvara! || 2 ||
O Ram-faced One, salutations to you, whose nature is that of Śiva and Śakti;
salutations to you, the embodiment of great wrath, who are mounted upon a ram.
Homage to you, Aśvasaṃvara, the god who leads horses, who delights in the act of passion, and who bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation. || 4 ||
Homage to you, O Vyāghrāsya; homage indeed to you who are endowed with power.
Homage to you, O Vyāghrasaṃvara, who are ever devoted to wine and meat. || 5 ||
Salutations to you, O Tortoise-faced One; salutations to you who are fully absorbed in sexual union.
Salutations to the God of gods; salutations to you, the Kūrmasaṃvara.
I bow to the one with the face of a fish, who indeed exists for the welfare of human beings;
salutations, salutations to you, O Lord of Gods; salutations to you, Matsyasaṃvara.
Salutations to you, O Makarasaṃvara, who have a mouth in the shape of a sea-monster, who wield great power, and who grant the desires of the mind. || 8 ||
Salutations to Saṃvara, who has the face of a camel, who embraces Śaktikā, and who is intent upon sexual union; O Uṣṭrasaṃvara, salutations to you!
I bow to the elephant-faced one, who bestows the *liṅga* within the womb;
salutations to you, O Blessed One, salutations to you, Gajasaṃvara.
Salutation to you, the Lord whose face is like a frog, the Sovereign of the three worlds;
salutation to the God of gods and to the one who is the vow of the frog.
I bow to the one who is without speech and eternally devoted to bliss;
homage to you, O Lord of the gods of gods, homage to you, Ahisaṃvara.
Homage, homage to you, the god with the face of a parrot, who is beautified by the form of the two aspects;
homage to you, O Bhīmāṅga, homage to you, Śukasaṃvara. || 13 ||
Salutations to you, the Restrainer; salutations indeed to you who are endowed with power. Salutations always to the lion-faced one; salutations to you, O Siṃhasaṃvara. || 14 ||
Salutations to you, O god with the face of a monkey, who delights in kissing the Śakti;
salutations to you, salutations to you, O Harisaṃvara, salutations to you! || 15 ||
O Dog-faced One, homage be to you, who kisses the Śakti;
homage to you, O Blessed Lord, O God, homage to you, the dog-restraint (Śvānasaṃvara).
O best of boar-faced ones, O you who cause the play of the Bhaga, I bow to you who are endowed with power; salutations to you, the restraint of friction. 17.
Salutations to the god Jambukāsya, to the one embraced by Śakti, to the remover of all sins, and to the vow of Śivā. || 18 ||
I bow to the one with the face of a vulture; homage to you who destroy suffering.
Homage to you, the deity who grants the accomplishment of the two forms, Gṛdhrasaṃvara! || 19 ||
Homage to you, the Blessed One, Kākānana, pure Yakṣa who assumes a form of passion; homage to you, Kākasaṃvara! || 20 ||
Homage to you, O Owl-faced One, the bestower of great bliss;
homage to you, the deity who engages in sexual union with the womb, O Owl-Saṃvara! (21)
Homage to you, the god with the face of Tārkṣya; homage to you, the savior from the ocean of existence; homage to you, Garuḍasaṃvara! 22.
Salutations to you whose face is like a cow's; salutations to the remover of the sin of cow-slaughter, to the bestower of increase to the lineage of cows, and to you who protect the cattle. || 23 ||
Salutations to you, the Lord of the Gaṇas, whose mouth has the form of a donkey, who has brought an end to coming and going, the divine one, the restraint of the ass. || 24 ||
Salutations to the god with the face of a buffalo, the cause of the great dissolution;
salutations to the god endowed with power, the subduer of Mahiṣa. 25.
Obeisance to you, Cat-Face, who sports in the pool of urine;
obeisance to the Supreme Lord, the most excellent one, O Mārjārasaṃvara.
I bow to the one whose face is Śālva, who shines as if with two bodies;
I bow to the Lord of the gods of gods; homage to Śarabhasaṃvara! 27.

Salutations to you, the perfected one, whose form is perfected; salutations to you, the virtuous one who abides in virtue; salutations to you, the Krauñca-faced one; salutations to you, the restrainer of Krauñca. || 28 ||
Homage, homage to the pure and supreme Ulkānana;
homage to you, O Ugra of terrifying form, O Ulkasaṃvara! || 29 ||
Obeisance to you, O Haṃsavaktra; obeisance to you whose very nature is the sound of the *haṃsa*;
obeisance to you whose form is "I am that" (*so 'ham*); obeisance to you, the restraint of the *haṃsa*.
I bow to the supreme lord, the god with the face of a deer;
salutations to you, O Mṛgasaṃvara, the bestower of supernatural powers and accomplishments. || 31 ||
Salutations to you who are endowed with power, and salutations to you whose face is like that of a ruddy goose; salutations to you, the vow known as Cakravāka, salutations again and again.
Homage to the Hero who brings about the cessation of ignorance and destroys nescience;
homage to you, O Unborn One, whose restraint leads to the attainment of the fruit of liberation. || 33 ||
Homage to you, the deity with the face of a cock, who increases the lineage;
homage to you, Kauṭukeśa, the vow of the cock. 34.
Salutations to you, whose face is like that of the black antelope, born of karma;
salutations to the divine destroyer of time, the protector of the deer. || 35 ||
Salutations again and again to the one with the crucible-face, who is full and bestows knowledge;
salutations to you, O Mūṣasaṃvara, the destroyer of all demons. || 36 ||
Salutations to you, O Sālūka; salutations to the bestower of honor and other boons;
and salutations to the giver of accomplishment and wisdom, O Sālūka-saṃvara.
Homage to the one whose face is upon his cheek, whose essential nature is wisdom and skillful means;
homage be to you, O Great Hero, and to Kapotasaṃvara. (38)
I bow to the one with the face of a crocodile, who bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation;
salutations be to you, O Lord of all beings, O Grāhasaṃvara, salutations to you!
Homage to you, O Cihlavaktra; homage to you, who delights in sexual union.
Homage to you, O Blessed Lord, O God; homage to you, Cihlasaṃvara. || 40 ||
Obeisance to you, the god whose face is like a sparrow; salutations to you, O Teacher of the World!
Salutations to you, O Lord of Virtues; obeisance to you, the restrainer of sparrows. || 41 ||
Homage to you, O Sarasāsya; homage to you, O ocean of virtues!
Homage to you, the Blessed One, and to the one who is the refuge of the Sarasas! 42.
Salutations to you, the god Khañjanāsya, the Great God (Mahādeva), the bestower of the state of Nirvāṇa, and the one whose vow is the Khañjarīṭa bird. || 43 ||
Salutations to you, the bringer of well-being, the bestower of both worldly enjoyment and liberation;
salutations to you, O Blessed Lord, the deity who is the sovereign bringer of well-being.
O Śaśākasya, homage to you; homage to you, O Lord of the World! Homage always to you, the bestower of karma; homage to Śaśakasamvara.
Homage to the one with the face of a bear, who is intent on the play of passion;
homage to the bestower of the accomplishment of all tasks, O Bhallūka-saṃvara! 46.
Homage to you, Pikāsya, who brings about the accomplishment of mantras;
homage to you, the Lord of the three worlds, the All-pervading One, Pikasaṃvara. || 47 ||
I bow to the one with the face of a crane, the Lord of Ganas joined with Śakti;
I bow to the Lord of the gods of gods, O Vakasaṃvara, homage be to you! 48.
Homage always with bowed head to the god Khaṅgivaktra;
homage be to the Supreme Lord, homage to you, Khaṅgisaṃvara. || 49 ||
O you with the face of a crab, homage to you; homage to the cause of cyclic existence!
Homage to the destroyer of the mass of sins, O Karkaṭasaṃvara! 50.
Homage to the one with the face of a porcupine, the remover of all defects;
homage to the destroyer of the snares of saṃsāra, to Śallakisaṃvara. 51.
Homage to you, O Scorpion-faced One, the bestower of strength and auspiciousness!
Homage, homage to you, the God; homage, O Scorpion-subduer! 52.
Salutation to you, the god with the face of a bee, who delights in bees;
salutation to you, the destroyer of the world of bees, the restraint of bees. || 53 ||
Homage be to you, O Jāhaka, who indeed causes delusion among people;
homage to the bestower of victory and auspiciousness, O Jāhakasaṃvara! 54.
O you whose face is like that of a yak, who constantly bestow the fruit of skillfulness, and who grant the four aims of human life—homage to you, O Camarisaṃvara! 55.
Salutations to you, Sīmnivaktra, the bestower of the fruit of spiritual accomplishment;
salutations eternally to the Blessed One, Sīmnisaṃvara, salutations to you.
I bow to the one with the face of a monitor lizard; salutations to you of terrible prowess!
Salutations to you with the divine eye; salutations to you, the restrainer of the monitor lizard! || 57 ||
O Cakora-faced one, salutations to you, the destroyer of the fault of fickleness;
salutations to you, the Blessed One, and to the protector of the cakora bird. || 58 ||
Homage to you, Godhikāsya, who constantly effects emanation and reabsorption;
homage to you, O Supreme Bliss, and to Godhikāsaṃvara. (59)
Homage to you, whose mouth is like honey-bees, O bestower of honor!
Homage to the omniscient Supreme Lord, O Mākṣikasaṃvara! 60.
O Pataṅgavaktra, O Supreme Lord, salutations to you always;
salutations to the divine Lord of Day, O Pataṅgasaṃvara! 61.
Homage to you, the god with the face of a man, the slayer of Naraka;
homage to you, O Narasaṃvara, who assumes manifold forms. || 62 ||
O abode of the world whose form is creation, you create all beings;
salutations, salutations to you eternally, and salutations to you, the source of both creation and its withdrawal.
Salutation to the God whose nature is stability, to the one who possesses qualities and who abides in the qualities; salutation to you, the destroyer of essence, O Lord of the restraint of stability!
O Supreme Lord, the agent of the dissolution of the entire world;
therefore, I bow down to You—salutations to You, the sovereign of the cosmic dissolution! 65.
O Jyotirvaktra, supreme abode, salutations to you, O Lord of the Universe! Salutations to you, the light more subtle than the most subtle, the concealment of all luminosity.
Thus, this hymn of Saṃvara is difficult to find in the three worlds;
it is a hymn superior to the most superior, consisting of sixty-four [verses].
Among the sixty-four [tantras], each preceding one is indeed more concise;
furthermore, because this work consists of many texts, only the very first has been set forth here.
One seeking a daughter obtains a daughter; one seeking wealth obtains wealth;
one seeking knowledge obtains knowledge; and one seeking liberation shall attain liberation. (69)
Subjugation, eradication, the delusion of Māra, immobilization, attraction, inciting enmity, alchemy, and elixirs; || 70 ||
The pill, the accomplishment of the sandals, and likewise the accomplishment of the sword;
the accomplishment of the sky-farer, the physician’s limb, and the accomplishment of mantra, as well as eloquence of speech. (71)
One obtains the power of entering another's body as well as the summoning of substances;
by means of this King of Hymns, this is truly so, truly so, as I have declared. (72)
During a famine or in times of adversity, one who performs the recitation shall obtain auspicious results;
likewise during excessive rain, drought, or the outbreak of a great pestilence.
In the event of the loss of a kingdom, the loss of knowledge, the loss of a wife, or the depletion of wealth; and in times of strife and dispute, one should recite this supreme hymn. (74)
The fruit produced by giving to thousands of mendicants is equal to the fruit born from the gift of the entire universe; what need is there for much speaking on this matter? (75)
In the *Śrīsaṃvarāgama*, the Great Tantra, in the dialogue between Amitābha and Vairocana, the *Śrīcakrasaṃvarādicatuḥṣaṣṭisaṃvarastotra* is completed.
